reviews.review:
I have 12 hours and have beaten the only current available route with the commando and engineer classes. and it's some of the most fun I have playing a game in a good while.

they make full use of the superhero comic motif that lets a dilapidated AK with a taped on grenade launcher and back alley jury-rigged energy gun feel in line with high-tech military rifles and a laser mini-gun. giving every gun distinct and identifiable features both mechanically and visually, going to far as to give them onomatopoeia when they shoot. all while playing this unstoppable armed doomguy-esque force of nature yet colorful, full-heatedly good robot simply called a guardian.

This game's roguelike aspect comes in the form of the weapons, affixes for these weapons, and cores that bump two of the 5 stats, and perks you gain from leveling up, all random to an extent. and progression comes in the form of upgrading your base camp, to let you get more/better weapon, perk and core options/rerolls throughout your run, as well as the 3 other guardian options and a series of gadgets you start every run. weapons have an affinity to one or two of the four stats that increases their damage when increased: assault, precision, demolition, or technology, with the 5th, robo, directly enhancing the guardian's key ability. and all stats have a secondary, more universal buff. these end up being the key to make one of many builds that let you be powerful that feels completely different with the same character, or interestingly similar to a different guardian type.

in the small slice of content available, they've made a game loop where every run feels different fun and unique, and as an early access game, it's already a blast to play. And I hope they can take it to the finish line.

and you can grind rails while firing a hitscan rocket launcher, if that's not the most mid 2000's radical thing you heard, then you're a chump.
hard to find singleplayer games this fun nowadays
